pr_title: [VideoPlayer] Fix and improve subtitle stream selection
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->
i started rework this part, starting from impaired problems and then i improved also other use cases

**problems fixed:**
1) if you set "original", kodi select and show the "forced" track based on audio language (ref. issue #25617)
2) "hearing impaired" setting dont works combined with "original"
3) "hearing impaired" setting apparently do nothing with "forced", now if both are enabled "forced" is internally disabled
4) if you set a sub language, and the video played dont have it, kodi still show a language based on audio language, that usually its different (does not comply with the chosen language), now if a sub language dont exists subtitles become disabled
5) "default" flag on all use cases was not so well handled, i handled some more distinctions on code
6) Changes to videos with embedded CC subtitles (read section below)
7) Wrong subs language selection can happens when: _audio language setting is set to a language not provided by the video played, and subtitle language setting is set to a language not provided by the video played or "forced"_. This will lead to a wrong subs language at playback startup. Caused by the fact that the code only considered the audio language coming from the audio track to be played without considering the audio language settings (ref. issue #15672)

### About subtitles "default" flag
from what i understood on the subtitles the "default" flag is not so important since it is used only
to give more priority to a stream, for the case when there are two streams with same properties (lang and flags, but maybe different author version or codec)
On kodi there is no “Media default” setting for subs in the GUI, such as happens on audio language setting, and there is no intention to implement it

### Note for the case 4
this problem was mentioned also on 
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/ed8f18b779b28ee62e5e1154e839479680612700/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoPlayer.cpp#L103
this behaviour make no sense to me, a user set a subtitle language because should want to display only that language, but kodi fallback to the audio language when missing, this does not match the GUI setting, this bug(?) or weird feature is not documented anywhere, so now has been changed, if the language is missing dont show nothing

### Changes to videos with embedded CC subtitles
The current behaviour of Kodi was:
on CC stream mark it as "hearing impaired", but on stream selection full ignore the "impaired" flag and treat it as regular subtitle

I find this behaviour inconsistent, that also make the subtitle selection code more hard to understand,
when a subtitle is defined/marked as “impaired” it should be treated as such, not force it with a different behavior

as also explained on wiki https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed_captioning CC subtitles are generally regular subtitles,
in some cases there may be countries that treat them for hearing impaired, but its not a rule.

what changes i have done: i removed the "impaired" flag previously set by default to CC streams. CC streams can be identified now by the "CC" name on description

![immagine](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/274a6863-806e-4c2b-b33b-741e675ca4e3)

the behavior remains the same as before,
plus i added a new setting that allows you to reassign the "impaired" flag to CC streams
![immagine](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29b4a9e3-bdbc-4020-9677-5d00250cf8f4)
this allows you to change the stream auto-selection behaviour of subtitles and can also prevent them from being automatically selected if not desired

the `language = "cc"` on `CDVDDemuxCC` demuxer has been removed
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/9f5b450620cc4fb284ea654ea4d71b3982af2b28/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/DVDDemuxers/DVDDemuxCC.cpp#L405
"cc" language code was sort of hack and an invalid lang code,
the only uses of "cc" lang was on the stream selection code that i have also removed since not needed anymore.
Instead of "cc" on CC will be set "und" thats an expected language code internally allowed for "undetermined" language case

### sidenotes
i removed the `subson` variable that was changing behaviour of the sort order (the order of priority) for unclear reasons to me,
if subtitles are disabled i dont see why there should be a different sort order
if some one has some reminescence of this say so, i found apparently no possible problems in its removal

I add missing Dhivehi to ISO 639-2, this lack wasted my time in testing, because caused different behavior in subtitle selection due to incorrect coversion of the language code, anyway the root of problem has been fixed by #26011

## Motivation and context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!--- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->
fix #25617
fix #24777
fix #15672

## How has this been tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your change. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
- basic things with self modified mkv that contains more subs
- mkv with more external subtitles (subs with same mkv filename but with appended "-eng-forced.srt", "-eng-impaired.srt", etc...),
- videos with embedded CC
- PVR iptv m3u with embedded CC

DVD is not affected by this PR change

pr_comments: As I understand it "forced" was created to mark certain portions of a sub for the original or primary audio track language.  Expanded to allow for an entire text codec sub to be treated as "forced", again for the original audio language and then expanded again for audio tracks in other languages as a separate "forced" text sub.   I guess the default is to show the "forced" sub if it exists for the current selected audio track language, irrespective of a global "enable sub" or "sub language" setting (unless player language subtitle set to "None").  But that probably cause problem where "forced" sub is separate from "narrative" or "hearing impaired" sub in the same language.  Not sure there is a correct answer.

forced are a type of subtitle tracks different from regular one, which show only a little info on the screen
not to be mixed with other tracks (avoid auto-selecting other types if “forced” is set)

>  I guess the default is to show the "forced" sub if it exists for the current selected audio track language, irrespective of a global "enable sub" or "sub language" setting (unless player language subtitle set to "None")

currently is not so...
is as i explained above, if there are duplicate subtitles with the exact same characteristics/properties those are selected
i think because there is no “Media default” setting for subs in the GUI, such as on audio language setting,
should be added the “Media default” setting to subs setting to do what you mean correctly,
I don't know the reason why there is no such setting for subtitles, perhaps because it would not be used much

## Bug report
Kodi automatically deactivates subtitles after a certain period of time. After manual reactivation in the Kodi OSD, the subtitles will be displayed again for a certain time until they are automatically deactivated again. I was able to understand the problem, especially with the PrimeVideo addon for adaptive streaming.
